adr: ADR-160 D7 — a force model declares the medium properties it requires and the media it is valid in; the envelope is declared by the model author, never inferred by the caller
mediaKnownWhy: The three media embodied's committed row implements, carried by this lab as data in medium-properties.json (ADR-160 D3: shared as data, never imported). This lab implements seawater with a free surface; it knows the other two by their rows and answers for nothing in them.
undeclared: FAILS CLOSED. A model with no entry here is treated as valid in this lab's default medium only and refuses every other medium by name (model_not_valid_in_medium). An undeclared envelope is the part most likely to be skipped, so its absence never reads as permission.

wave-propulsion.label: Wave propulsion (engine/wave/wave-propulsion.ts)
wave-propulsion.why: Its lift is the panel method's (inviscid, the same in any fluid) and its drag a Reynolds correlation, so the force terms are not what exclude air: the kinematic ceiling U_max = w_heave / tan(beta_stop) is medium-independent. What air lacks is the free surface the float heaves on, and asking for heave there is medium_property_unavailable: freeSurface, never a quiet zero. A vacuum has no fluid at all (density zero, no Reynolds number, no lift), so the model declines it by this envelope.
